races.name: Pink Lady Find Your Fizz Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Kokanee
runners_data.note: Ed Dunlop's 4yo has not run since April (48 days) and his recent form at 8-10f on Good/Soft is on shorter ground than today's 10f AW trip; a genuine hold-up horse whose natural rear position is compressed by the volume of closers in this field, further limiting his scope to get a clean run.
runners_data.comment: Landed a win two starts back but has struggled either side of it, and 48 days off adds a fitness query; has run over today's distance and going, though an eighth last time out tempers expectations carrying 134 lb from stall 2.

runners_data.name: Pomme Pomme
runners_data.note: The race's lone front-runner and the key pace-setter, Jack Channon's filly has just one win and one place from 14 Standard-going runs but controls the tactical shape entirely; Rose Dawes claims 5lb which lightens her burden, and her form line shows she stays the trip.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked eighth of nine on our figures, Pomme Pomme makes this a tough sell, though she does bring distance and going experience to the table and a third last time out offers a sliver of encouragement after 27 days off.

runners_data.name: Moonrunner
runners_data.note: Charlie Fellowes' lightly-raced 4yo has placed at 12f on Soft/Standard and showed form at Lingfield's AW (3/11f/STA), suggesting the track and trip suit — true running style is rear-of-field but the crowded hold-up division means he will be pushed wider than ideal in the early stages.
runners_data.comment: Consistent performer who has finished second and third in recent starts, Moonrunner has experience of today's trip and conditions and a rating of 84 suggests he is ahead of the handicapper, though 72 days off the track and a winless recent run of form are the risks to factor in.

runners_data.name: Skibo
runners_data.note: Off 117 days and wearing headgear (h), Barry Brennan's 4yo has placed twice at 10f on Good ground and is a hold-up horse by trade; the lengthy absence plus an already compressed back-field make it hard to see him getting the race to unfold on his terms.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and 117 days off the track are the concerns, though a second and a third in recent starts show he can be competitive; has run over today's trip and going, and carries 129 lb from stall 3.

runners_data.name: Mwafaq
runners_data.note: Fahey's 4yo is in sparkling form — 152112 — and has won and placed repeatedly at 7-8f on Good and Soft, stepping up to 10f today on AW; races prominently (headgear: p), which is the prime tactical seat in this moderate-pace scenario, and the 5lb claimer Tindall keeps the weight manageable.
runners_data.comment: Ranked last of nine on our figures, Mwafaq faces a stiff ask on ratings, though his recent form reads well — a winner two starts back and a runner-up last time out 21 days ago — and he has experience on today's going.

runners_data.name: Orchard
runners_data.note: Warren Greatrex has had no winners in 9 runners over 14 days, and Luke Morris partners a horse whose natural style is rearward; has won at 8f/Standard and placed at 10f/Good, giving distance and going credentials, but races out of his preferred position in this field configuration.
runners_data.comment: Ranked seventh of nine on our figures, Orchard looks a tough sell despite consecutive placed efforts last time out and two starts back; he has experience over today's trip and returns after a 28-day break, but the ratings gap makes him hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Cloth Of Gold
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's team is in solid form (7/40 in 14 days) and Jonny Peate rides a 4yo who has placed five times in ten Standard-going runs, showing consistent AW form at 10-11f — a genuine hold-up operator whose best chance comes in a scenario where pace generates a strong finishing burst.
runners_data.comment: Cloth Of Gold arrives here just 16 days since his last outing, fit and ready, with experience of today's distance and going in his favour and a speed rating of 88 underscoring his latent ability; yet to score in his last five starts, the main risk is whether he can convert that promise into a win.

runners_data.name: Epictetus
runners_data.note: Jamie Osborne's 6yo has been placed in six of his last 15 Good-ground starts and most recently won over 10f/Good, with healthy recent form (305231); races from hold-up but has the profile to be competitive if the race produces a late dash, though he has not reproduced his best on AW Standard.
runners_data.comment: Epictetus won last time out and, with experience of today's trip and conditions already banked, he looks the one to beat off 137 lb from stall seven, his rating of 86 putting him top of our list.

runners_data.name: Wanderlust
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's 4yo (headgear: p) ran just 15 days ago and has a record of placing consistently at 10-12f; Tom Queally is a significant booking and the horse's prominent-leaning style means he could slot in behind Pomme Pomme to exploit the controlled gallop, though going-to-hand Standard form is thin (0W1P from 8 runs).
runners_data.comment: Wanderlust brings solid recent form to the table — third two starts back and a winner five starts back — and has run over today's trip, returning fit on just 15 days' rest carrying 136 lb from stall one. The fifth last time out is the one blemish to overcome.

races.paceDynamic: Pomme Pomme is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rivals to press her early, she is virtually guaranteed to control the pace from the front on Standard Polytrack at Lingfield's 1m2f trip. With a field dominated by hold-up types, Pomme Pomme will dictate a sustainable, uncontested gallop that is unlikely to be truly searching — the sort of pace that rewards those able to travel close to the tempo and pounce rather than those relying on a strong end-to-end gallop to bring them into it. The field holds significantly more hold-up types than the race shape can naturally accommodate: Kokanee, Moonrunner, Skibo, and Orchard are all genuine rear-division horses who are mapped to midfield simply because there is no room for them all at the back — their chances are materially discounted in a shape that requires them to race in their true role. The tactical verdict is clear: prominent runners and versatile stalkers who can sit just off Pomme Pomme's easy lead and produce a sharp turn of foot into the home straight will be most favoured; deep closers need a pace they are unlikely to get.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pomme Pomme Controls, Stalkers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Pomme Pomme sets an uncontested, moderate gallop and prominent raiders time their move off her entering the straight.
scenarios.body: Mwafaq and Wanderlust, both capable of racing prominently, can track the leader comfortably and produce a decisive late effort having been placed to pounce; the steady tempo into the straight suits those with tactical speed rather than raw stamina.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, In-Running Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Pomme Pomme sets a truly dawdling gallop that compresses the field and produces a cavalry charge in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Horses with raw ability and strong finishing kicks — Epictetus and Cloth Of Gold — would benefit from the late-burst nature, and their Standard going form at this sort of trip makes them credible beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pomme Pomme Front-To-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If the pace she sets turns out to be stronger than expected and the hold-up brigade are caught flat-footed coming off the home bend.
scenarios.body: Pomme Pomme has won and placed at this trip range and, if she steals enough of a lead turning in without being challenged, Mwafaq from a prominent pitch is best placed to give chase while the back-markers simply run out of track.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens significantly mid-race, creating genuine end-to-end fractions that bring closers into play in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely shape given only one natural front-runner, but if it materialises Kokanee or Moonrunner — genuine hold-up types who would need to overcome their out-of-role map positions — would theoretically benefit, though the structural disadvantage caps confidence sharply.

watchPoints.text: Mwafaq has winning form at 8f on multiple going types and arrives in career-best form (152112) — if he secures a prominent pitch just off Pomme Pomme's lead, he enters the straight in the best tactical position and represents the most dangerous profile in this pace shape.

Pomme Pomme's single confirmed front-running role means any hesitation at the start or a challenge for the lead from a jockey keen to be positive would fundamentally alter the race shape — watch the early stalls break to see if she goes straight to the front.

Wanderlust has Tom Queally booked — a jockey who often improves horses tactically — and if Queally places him close to the pace rather than in his natural hold-up role, the horse's consistent placed form over this trip could make him harder to dismiss.

Kokanee, Moonrunner, Skibo, and Orchard are all genuine hold-up horses competing for limited real estate at the back of this field — whichever of them draws the clearest passage into the home straight from the outside will have the best chance of the group, but none should be assumed to get their preferred run.

Cloth Of Gold carries the joint-top weight (137lbs) alongside Epictetus despite an OR of 82, and five placed runs from ten Standard outings suggest AW competence — worth monitoring in-running for any sign of a sustained staying-on effort if the pace compresses the field in the closing stages.

races.name: North Downs Hospital Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Notable Charm
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer for Marcus Tregoning returning after 28 days, but her AW form reads poorly (0W0P in 5 Standard runs) and she has shown no ability to win from the back at this trip; the 1m4f looks a stretch based on recent form string of 09646.
runners_data.comment: Notable Charm has been winless in his last five starts, with a fourth two runs back offering the sole bright spot, and he carries a testing 133 lb here; experience of today's going helps, but he has plenty to find on ratings.

runners_data.name: Naranka
runners_data.note: George Baker's filly won over 12f at Goodwood on her penultimate start and placed again over the same trip, giving her strong claims on a stamina basis; Pat Cosgrave takes over after 52 days off and, unusually for this field, she has a realistic profile to close from hold-up into a steady pace if positioned close enough.

runners_data.name: Pepper Fizz
runners_data.note: Gina Mangan rides for Georgina Nicholls after a 75-day absence, and the form string of 95-606 offers little encouragement; the AW Standard record shows 0W0P in one comparable run and the longer trip of 1m4f has not been tried before, raising a question mark over stamina.
runners_data.comment: Pepper Fizz heads into this winless in her last five starts, but our rating puts her clear at the top of these nine and she carries her 133 lb with a 75-day break to shake off — one to respect if freshness unlocks more.

runners_data.name: Amalou
runners_data.note: Daniel & Claire Kubler's charge returns from a lengthy 269-day absence — the longest layoff in the field — and carries a 'fades in finish' flag alongside an AW record showing 0W0P in two Standard runs; her true running style is hold-up, though the redistribution places her in midfield, and ring-rustiness after nine months off is the primary concern.
runners_data.comment: Amalou carries a hefty 132 lb and returns after 269 days off the track, which raises a fitness query, but she has experience of today's going and our rating puts her ahead of her official mark — the main risk is whether that long absence blunts her comeback bid.

runners_data.name: Angel Breeze
runners_data.note: Tongued-tied for Lemos De Souza, this hold-up filly was last seen just 17 days ago when placed third over 10f at Goodwood, which is the most encouraging piece of recent form in the field; she fades in the finish flag tempers enthusiasm despite the freshness, and she will need the pace to be strong enough to allow a late run that the race shape may not provide.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Angel Breeze faces a stiff task at 131 lb, though she has run over today's going before and was third last time out.

runners_data.name: Turton
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll sends out this hold-up type who has failed to win or place in five similar-going runs, with a form string of 86956 suggesting consistent mid-pack finishes without ever threatening; William Carson takes the ride but the redistribution to midfield reflects his true rearward style, and no significant positive angle stands out.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked eighth of nine on our figures, Turton is hard to fancy on recent form — consecutive finishes of sixth, fifth, ninth, sixth and eighth paint a bleak picture — though he has run over today's going before and returns after a 31-day break.

runners_data.name: Cormorant Rock
runners_data.note: Jim Boyle's runner was out just 8 days ago and carries the lowest OR in the field at 45, partnered by claimer Donagh Murphy; his history shows repeated top-five finishes over 10f at Goodwood but no win or placed finish on AW Standard in comparable conditions, and the redistribution confirms he would naturally be further back than the map suggests.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, with a ninth last time out his most recent contribution, Cormorant Rock faces a stiff task ranked seventh of nine on our figures, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a quick eight-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Crazy Plan
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner for Dan Horsford, Kieren Fox takes over and the horse has placed twice in five Standard AW runs including a second over 12f here, giving him genuine course and distance form; he will enjoy a soft lead, though the STYLE_FIT flag is a mild caveat suggesting he may not be a pure out-and-out leader who thrives on complete domination.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Crazy Plan nonetheless shaped with promise when second two runs back, and having run over today's trip and going she should not lack for adaptability; the 135 lb burden, however, looks a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Lady Of Clover
runners_data.note: George Scott's filly boasts the best overall profile in the field with a win on AW Standard ground over 8f and a form string of 363143 showing consistent competitiveness; Liam Wright (5lb claimer) partners her, she wears headgear and was last seen 50 days ago, but she has AW experience and is the most likely of the redistributed hold-up types to secure a forward enough position to contest the finish.
runners_data.comment: Lady Of Clover shaped with credit when third last time out, and a winner three starts back; she has experience of today's going and our rating puts her ahead of her official mark, making her a genuine threat — the 50-day absence is the one factor to weigh.

runners_data.name: Dijon Gone
runners_data.note: Denis Coakley's runner returns after 82 days and carries a 'fades in finish' flag, with a form string of 6-0087 and no AW Standard wins or places in five relevant runs; Rose Dawes (5lb) claims, and while he is mapped to midfield due to redistribution, his true style is hold-up and the finishing fade tendency makes this shape particularly unflattering for him.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and absent for 82 days, Dijon Gone nevertheless catches the eye on our rating of 58 against an official mark of 52, suggesting she holds more ability than her recent form implies — the fitness question after nearly three months off is the chief concern.

races.paceDynamic: Crazy Plan is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner field and, with no rival likely to press him hard from the gates, he can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over the 1m4f Lingfield AW trip on Standard ground. The remainder of the field is overwhelmingly held-up or prominent in style, meaning the pace is likely to be modest and metronomic rather than searching, which plays directly into the hands of a horse that can travel comfortably on the front end. With no genuine second or third string to push Crazy Plan off his rhythm, closers will face the classic flat-track dilemma: a clean, uncontested lead often means there is no pace collapse late, narrowing the window for hold-up horses to reel him in. This race shape firmly favours a well-positioned prominent racer or a horse comfortable tracking a lone leader just off the pace, rather than deep hold-up types who need a strong gallop to close into. Several redistributed runners — notably Lady Of Clover, Dijon Gone, Amalou and Angel Breeze — are true hold-up horses placed in midfield on the map because the field cannot accommodate every rearward style; of those, Lady Of Clover, with her AW winning form, is most likely to secure a forward enough position to matter.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Crazy Plan Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Crazy Plan bowls along in front uncontested and the steady pace never truly accelerates until late.
scenarios.body: Crazy Plan dictates every yard at a comfortable clip, depriving hold-up horses of the strong gallop they need to close, and his rivals are left with too much ground to make up in the straight; horses closest to him through the race enjoy the clearest path to the prize.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse tracks Crazy Plan at close range throughout and outstays him inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The steady pace means the leader does not empty early, but a fresh hold-up or prominent type sitting a length or two off the pace can use the slipstream and pounce late with a short, sharp burst; the longer 1m4f trip rewards a horse who has conserved energy behind the leader.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Crazy Plan sets an uncharacteristically strong early pace or quickens sharply, burning himself out before the straight.
scenarios.body: A genuine pace collapse would open the door for hold-up horses sweeping through from midfield, but given the field's style redistribution this depends on horses racing out of their natural role, reducing the likelihood materially; Naranka and Lady Of Clover, having winning or placed form at this trip, are best positioned to benefit.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Blanket Finish, No Clear Winner
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so even and slow that multiple horses arrive together in the straight with nothing between them.
scenarios.body: A truly compressed finish becomes possible if Crazy Plan idles in front and several midfield horses close in unison without a dominant finisher emerging; given the moderate ratings and lack of course specialist depth, an edgy, tight finish is a minor possibility but the weight of evidence points elsewhere.

watchPoints.text: Crazy Plan and Kieren Fox — if they are allowed to bowl along unchallenged at their own rhythm, the race may effectively be over turning for home; watch whether any horse attempts to go with him early, as no rival doing so makes the front ideal territory.

Lady Of Clover (Liam Wright) — mapped to midfield but a genuine hold-up type with AW winning form; watch where she actually positions at the start, as breaking prominently would significantly upgrade her chance in this slow-pace scenario.

Angel Breeze (Luke Morris) — the most recent runner in the field and last seen placing at Goodwood, but the 'fades in finish' flag combined with a steady pace from Crazy Plan means she may find herself tracking without the strong gallop she needs to close; watch her position through the early stages.

Naranka (Pat Cosgrave) — 52 days off but the only horse in the field with back-to-back top-two finishes at 12f, giving her a stamina edge; if Cosgrave slots her in second or third early, she becomes the most dangerous late threat to Crazy Plan.

Amalou — a 269-day absence is the standout fitness flag; watch her behaviour in the paddock and early in the race, as a ring-rusty run after nine months would be unsurprising regardless of form or position.

races.name: Advance Online Digital Media Group Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Hebridean Nomad
runners_data.note: Excellent Standard All-Weather record (12 runs, 2W7P) and has placed at 1m3f-1m4f; Alfie Redman's 7lb claim is meaningful at these weights, and tracking Mountbatten from a prominent pitch is his natural game — 182 days off is the only question mark.
runners_data.comment: Hebridean Nomad bounced back to win two starts back and followed up with a runner-up finish last time, suggesting he is in fine fettle, and he has run over today's trip and going before; the 182-day absence is the one query on this otherwise appealing profile.

runners_data.name: Betelgeuse
runners_data.note: Has placed twice over 1m6f-2m on Good and showed stamina credentials at Goodwood, but his natural style is deep hold-up; in this race he is likely to find himself closer than ideal to the pace, which may actually help over this trip if he can settle behind Mountbatten in transit — headgear noted.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Betelgeuse is ranked fifth of six on our figures and his speed rating trails his rating, making him hard to fancy despite carrying a workable weight and having run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Last Verse
runners_data.note: Highest-rated runner at OR 75 and won over 1m2f on Good ground; all form is on Goodwood Good, so the Standard AW surface is an unknown quantity, though his trainer Joseph Parr has had no runners in form over 14 days and the 3yo faces older rivals stepping markedly up in trip.
runners_data.comment: Third two starts back and a winner three starts back, Last Verse arrives on a sharp 14-day turnaround with distance experience and our ratings marking him as the pick of the field; that tame ninth last time out is the one note of caution.

runners_data.name: Mountbatten
runners_data.note: The race's lone confirmed front-runner; Sir Mark Prescott's record with hold-up-to-front-running horses is well established, and Mountbatten won over 1m2f on Standard before placing over 1m4f — Luke Morris will likely exploit the uncontested lead at a trip that should suit.
runners_data.comment: Mountbatten ran a fine race last time out, finishing second, and that run came on the back of a win three starts back — he has experience of today's distance and going, and a speed rating of 77 underlines his claims. The risk is that his fourth two starts back suggests some inconsistency.

runners_data.name: Last Trump
runners_data.note: Three runs only, all on soft or Good, and 74 days since last seen; Marcus Tregoning is in low form (1/9 over 14 days), and the unexposed 3yo faces a significant surface and trip question stepping onto Standard AW over 1m5f for the first time.
runners_data.comment: Last Trump has run over today's trip and his speed rating of 79 gives him a strong case as a leading danger in this field, with our rating of 73 putting him ahead of the official assessment — though 74 days off the track and a winless recent run of three starts are the chief concerns.

runners_data.name: Virtue Diligence
runners_data.note: Amanda Perrett's 3yo has no Standard AW form in five runs (0W0P on similar going) and showed an 8th from 9 runners in her most recent outing; a genuine hold-up type who is likely to be closer to the pace than she prefers given the limited field size, which works against her usual pattern.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Virtue Diligence has little to recommend him at the weights, though he has run over today's trip before and the third two starts back at least shows a flicker of form.

races.paceDynamic: Mountbatten is the sole confirmed front-runner in a six-horse field at 1m5f on Lingfield's All-Weather, and with no rivals likely to press him from the outset, Luke Morris can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop throughout. Hebridean Nomad will track closely from a prominent position, but the remainder — Last Verse, Last Trump, Betelgeuse and Virtue Diligence — are all natural hold-up horses who will be racing off Mountbatten's pace from varying distances behind. This field holds more genuine hold-up types than can all secure their preferred rear-tracking position; Betelgeuse and Virtue Diligence are redistributed to midfield on the map because Last Verse and Last Trump are equally likely to occupy the back of the field, and in practice several will be bunched closer than ideal. A lone front-runner controlling a steady Standard-surface gallop over 1m5f strongly favours the lead-and-prominent profile: Mountbatten dictating and Hebridean Nomad tracking within striking range are the chief tactical beneficiaries, while the closers face the classic risk of a pace that never truly stretches before the turn for home.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Mountbatten Controls, Wires
scenarios.trigger: If Mountbatten gets an uncontested lead and sets a measured gallop that the hold-up pack cannot adequately close on.
scenarios.body: Mountbatten dictates every fraction from the front, with Luke Morris able to conserve energy and lengthen when asked in the straight; Sir Mark Prescott's patient framing of a horse who won over 1m2f on Standard and has placed over 1m4f suits this distance step perfectly. Hebridean Nomad, tracking just behind on similar Standard going with two wins and seven places in comparable conditions, is best placed of the chasers to capitalise if Mountbatten weakens.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Mountbatten's pace is just fast enough to stretch the field but Hebridean Nomad times a challenge to collar him in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Hebridean Nomad has an excellent record on Standard All-Weather (12 runs, 2 wins, 7 places) and his recent 1m2f and 1m4f form suggests the step to 1m5f is within range for a horse who stays strongly; Alfie Redman's claim reduces the weight burden and could prove the marginal edge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closer Delivers Late
scenarios.trigger: If Mountbatten sets an unexpectedly strong pace that brings hold-up horses into play at the business end.
scenarios.body: Last Verse, despite mostly Goodwood form, won over 1m2f on Good and has shown the ability to quicken; at OR 75 he is the highest-rated runner and if the pace genuinely stretches the field he has the class to finish powerfully. Betelgeuse and Virtue Diligence are both racing out of their natural deep-tracking position having been redistributed to midfield, which tempers confidence in their ability to deliver a true late thrust.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Bunched Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Mountbatten sets an unusually slow tempo that compresses the field and produces a sprint finish from the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: A genuinely slow gallop would neutralise Mountbatten's tactical advantage and open the race to any runner who can quicken off a flat pace, favouring Last Verse's class and Last Trump's fresh-legged profile after 74 days off; however this scenario requires Mountbatten to race entirely out of character and is the least likely shape given Prescott's typical front-running instructions.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Hebridean Nomad's 182-day absence has left him short of peak fitness — if he is slightly ring-rusty he may fade having tracked Mountbatten early, handing the race back to the leader.

Monitor Virtue Diligence's starting position and early movement: her true hold-up style will be compressed in a six-runner field, and if she is pushed forward against her nature the race shape changes for the closers behind.

Betelgeuse is similarly a natural rear-tracker who may find himself in uncharacteristically close contact with the pace — if he over-races in the first mile his stamina could be undermined rather than maximised.

Last Trump is 74 days off the track with no Standard AW experience; Gina Mangan rides, and an unexposed 3yo returning fresh on an unfamiliar surface over 1m5f could run to a very different level than her handicap mark suggests in either direction.

Check for any Lingfield AW bias signals on the night — the Standard going report is consistent across all distances, but if the inside rail is riding fast it would further entrench Mountbatten's advantage as the likely rail-hugging leader.

races.name: Spa At The Marriott Lingfield Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Bands B, C And D) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Shemiyla Star
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's filly has solid course-and-distance form (placed twice at Goodwood), handles this going, and steps back up from 6f; her natural style is deep hold-up, but with several genuine closers in the field she may struggle to find the position she needs, tempering confidence in her finishing run.

runners_data.name: Xochipilli
runners_data.note: Unraced and a complete unknown for Loughnane, who has a modest 14-day strike rate; without any form or going data, all assessment is speculative, though being drawn in this field on debut at 7f on turf means raw ability alone must compensate for experience.

runners_data.name: Pirates Paradise
runners_data.note: George Scott's debutant showed some promise finishing fifth over 7f at Goodwood — a trip that suits here — and the yard fires in winners selectively; naturally a hold-up type who could benefit if the pace is genuine enough to bring him into contention late.

runners_data.name: Planet Bluebird
runners_data.note: Debuting for Mark Usher, who has a low 14-day strike rate and limited firepower; no going, form or style profile to work from, so the risk is high, though a longer trip like 7f on turf could suit a horse whose stable targets maiden opportunities carefully.

runners_data.name: Casablanca Dream
runners_data.note: The only confirmed pace-setter in the race, last seen finishing sixth over 6f at Goodwood; steps up to 7f here where she can make all at a comfortable tempo — her STYLE_FIT flag suggests she may be fractionally out of her natural role but in a field this weak for pace, she has the lead to herself.

runners_data.name: Remember The Show
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's colt finished a distant ninth over 7f at Goodwood last time and carries a fades-in-finish warning; hold-up style is noted but the finishing effort has not been convincing, and it is hard to make a case for improvement on current form.

runners_data.name: Mount St
runners_data.note: George Boughey's filly ran a solid third over 7f at Goodwood, handles turf and this trip well, and Grace McEntee takes a positive booking; natural hold-up style suits the pace shape here and third over a similar trip last time (8 days ago) means fitness is not an issue.

runners_data.name: Purple Dream
runners_data.note: Tom Ward's filly has two runs to her name including a twelfth on Lingfield AW on similar going — zero wins and zero places on that surface — making her profile difficult to support; hold-up style means she needs pace, which is thin in this race.

runners_data.name: Starlight Bay
runners_data.note: Unraced for Marcus Tregoning, a trainer who can produce smart debutants; no form, going preference or style profile exists, so the assessment is entirely speculative, though Tregoning's patient approach with juveniles means she could be better prepared than market position suggests.

runners_data.name: Brondesbury
runners_data.note: Loughnane's runner has finished tenth and twelfth in two runs — both fading — and carries a fades-in-finish flag; his true style is hold-up but with the rear of the field congested and his form deeply unconvincing, he is hard to fancy even if he finds a clear run.

runners_data.name: Call Of The Sea
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's colt ran eighth over 7f at Goodwood (42 days ago, so fresh) and his true running style is at the back of the field; the redistribution note means he is likely to find himself further off the pace than ideal, and the fades-in-finish flag on a horse who has not threatened yet limits the case.

runners_data.name: Eighth Immortal
runners_data.note: Luke Morris aboard this Jack Jones-trained colt who has placed in three of three starts (2-3-3) and carries headgear; consistent form at 7f and 6f on turf, handles the going, and the upward trajectory of form with experience makes him the most exposed positive profile in the race.

runners_data.name: Norham
runners_data.note: Adam Kirby-trained (trainer doubles as jockey) debutant who ran fourth over 5f at Goodwood — a notably different trip — and must now handle 7f for the first time; Tom Queally is a useful booking and the Goodwood run showed ability, but the stamina question at this longer trip is real.

races.paceDynamic: Casablanca Dream is the only confirmed front-runner in this 13-runner field and, having finished sixth over 6f at Goodwood last time, steps up to 7f where she can dictate an uncontested, controlled tempo on Standard Lingfield turf. With no rival likely to challenge her for the lead, the pace will be honest but sustainable — neither a crawl nor a burn-up — creating a single-file procession that rewards horses travelling smoothly in behind rather than those fighting for position. The absence of a second genuine pace-setter means the fractions will be measured, with the field strung out through the long Lingfield straight, suiting horses that can settle mid-race and produce a one-run finish rather than those needing a truly strong gallop to get competitive. This shape firmly favours hold-up horses with proven stamina for 7f and a clean run into the straight — runners like Mount St, Shemiyla Star and Eighth Immortal fit that profile best. Three runners — Call Of The Sea, Brondesbury and Shemiyla Star — are genuine hold-up types that the map has redistributed to midfield because the rear of the field is over-subscribed; of those, Casablanca Dream is virtually certain to secure the front, while the redistributed trio will need to find room from further back than their natural style demands.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Casablanca Dream Controls Comfortably
scenarios.trigger: If Casablanca Dream leads without pressure and sets a fair, uncontested gallop that suits a prominent-to-midfield closer.
scenarios.body: Casablanca Dream dictates through the first half and the pace stays manageable, meaning the winner comes from a horse that tracked her at close quarters and had a clear run entering the final 2f; the long straight rewards those who quicken from a handy position rather than deep closers held too far back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Strike Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is slightly stronger than expected and the field spreads wide in the straight, allowing horses from the back half to pick off tiring rivals.
scenarios.body: A modestly stronger tempo stretches the field through the dip and into the straight, giving genuine hold-up horses enough time to close; runners who settled well off the pace and have 7f stamina come into their own in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Debut/Lightly Raced Runner Bolts Up
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three unraced runners — Xochipilli, Planet Bluebird or Starlight Bay — is significantly better than any horse in this field on home gallops and produces a dominant performance on debut.
scenarios.body: A well-prepared debutant goes forward or travels powerfully through the race and proves too good for exposed rivals; the open maiden conditions and restricted band mean a classy unexposed type can dominate without a true test.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Front Runner Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is genuinely slow and the field gathers into a sprint in the final 2f, leaving Casablanca Dream's advantage intact through the line.
scenarios.body: If no hold-up horse manages to close the gap quickly enough through a falsely run race, Casablanca Dream's uncontested lead proves decisive; this is the least likely shape given the field size and the number of runners that will be hunting her down.

watchPoints.text: Casablanca Dream has the lead to herself — watch whether Jack Gilligan bowls along at a true gallop or slows the tempo in the first 3f, as this single decision will determine whether hold-up horses can close or whether the race is run as a procession.

Mount St and Eighth Immortal are the two most consistent hold-up types with proven 7f form — watch where they settle in the first furlong, as a clean position 3-5 lengths off the leader is the key requirement for either to land this race.

Call Of The Sea, Brondesbury and Shemiyla Star are all genuine closers pushed into the middle of the field by congestion — watch the early stages to see whether any of them gets outpaced and ends up further back than the map shows, which would effectively remove them from contention.
Eighth Immortal's headgear is worth noting — if it sharpens his early speed he may travel closer to the pace than his style label suggests, which would improve his chance in the dominant race shape.

The three debutants (Xochipilli, Planet Bluebird, Starlight Bay) should be monitored in the market before post time — any significant last-minute support for any of them, particularly from yards with a record of placing well-prepared juveniles, would upgrade Scenario C meaningfully.

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Daring Legend
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator with a 42-day break and bleak recent form (five runs yielding one place, no win); limited course-and-surface exposure (3 from 15 on similar going, no wins) and a sprint background on good ground make this trip and surface a concern, with no obvious tactical angle to exploit the pace shape.

runners_data.name: Arctician
runners_data.note: The only genuine front-runner in the field, and with 13 starts on similar going and two wins at course and distance, his ability to dictate an uncontested gallop is the defining tactical fact of this race; trainer Simon Dow has saddled a winner in the past 14 days and the horse returns on a quick 10-day turnaround suggesting he is in a productive spell.

runners_data.name: Madame De Sevigne
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse — her trainer John Butler has been in good recent form (6/27 in 14 days) — but she is genuinely racing out of her preferred position in this shape, with good-ground form flattering and a mixed record (0W, 3P) on similar surfaces; the style-fit discount applies and she needs the pace to collapse to fire.
runners_data.comment: Ranked top of the field on our rating and carrying 133 lb from stall 2, Madame De Sevigne has experience of today's trip and conditions and arrives here fresh after 28 days off, though she remains winless in her last six starts and that is the concern.

runners_data.name: Lady Manzor
runners_data.note: Remarkably consistent in placing (four consecutive fourths, including multiple times on this surface) but has not won since stepping up to this class, and with 73 days since her last outing she faces a fitness question; her true hold-up style is squeezed out by the field's composition, meaning she must race closer than ideal to the pace.
runners_data.comment: Lady Manzor has run over today's trip and going before and her speed rating of 81 suggests she holds solid claims as a leading danger here, but four consecutive fourths in recent starts leave her yet to score, and converting that consistency into a win remains the key question.

runners_data.name: Moon Beginnings
runners_data.note: Carries a cautionary flag for fading in the finish, and her form profile — 0W, 1P from 10 runs on similar going — makes this surface unreliable for her; the headgear (t) may sharpen her early, but as a genuine closer forced towards midfield by the field's composition, she is unlikely to get the strongly-run race she needs.
runners_data.comment: Moon Beginnings is winless in his last six starts, though a fourth three starts back offers some encouragement; he has run over today's distance and going before and returns after 20 days, but the weight of 129 lb from stall five may not help his cause.

runners_data.name: Timely Affair
runners_data.note: The form horse in the race — three wins and six places from 12 starts on similar going, including a course-and-distance win — and the headgear (p) has been in place during that successful spell; as a natural hold-up horse, the moderate solo pace is not ideal, but her tactical versatility makes her the likeliest to push forward and exploit the slow tempo off the pace.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of seven on our figures, Timely Affair faces a stiff ask here, though he has run over today's trip and going before and arrives in decent heart after winning last time out, with a return to form from stall one after 30 days off offering slim hope.

runners_data.name: Mollie Foster
runners_data.note: A course and distance winner but has run six consecutive sixths since that win, suggesting she has been found out at this level; her natural hold-up style is at least authentic, and on the surface where she scored, she remains the most credible late-closer if the pace shapes up to suit — though the losing run is impossible to ignore.
runners_data.comment: Mollie Foster's sole recent win came five starts back, and she brings distance and going experience into this, with our rating of 78 putting her right in contention from stall 3; the concern is four consecutive sixth-place finishes since that victory.

runners_data.name: Dannick
runners_data.note: A course-and-distance winner on this surface (sim-going 9/15, 1W, 5P) and equipped with headgear (tv) which has featured in his best efforts; Tom Queally is an experienced handler of course-specific races, and Dannick is among the most likely of the redistributed hold-up types to push forward and sit prominently — the position from which he won his course race.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom but one on our figures and rated below his official mark, Dannick faces a stiff ask, though second last time out and a winner two starts back at least show he retains some ability, and he has run over today's trip and going before.

races.paceDynamic: Arctician is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will stride to the front from the gates and control the tempo over Lingfield's flat polytrack mile entirely on his own terms. James Glennon's mount has run 13 of 15 career starts on similar going and posted back-to-back placed efforts at this course and distance, meaning he will set a measured, sustainable gallop rather than a suicidal one — creating a rail-hugging, compressed race with minimal mid-race surge. The rest of the field — Dannick, Madame De Sevigne, Lady Manzor, Timely Affair, Moon Beginnings, Daring Legend and Mollie Foster — are all natural hold-up or prominent types, and the field contains far more of them than the track map can accommodate at the rear; Timely Affair and Dannick, each proven over this course and surface, are likeliest to push forward and secure a prominent berth behind Arctician, leaving the others to jostle in a congested midfield. A solo, uncontested leader setting a fair pace over one mile on a flat, standard-condition polytrack strongly favours a prominent-to-mid racer with a sharp turn of foot who can track the pace and strike inside the final two furlongs, rather than a deep hold-up horse that needs a strong gallop to reel in the field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Arctician Leads, Tracker Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Arctician's uncontested, moderate gallop stretches the field into a strung-out line and a prominent tracker picks off the leader in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Arctician dictates from the front at a controlled pace, meaning the race is won by a horse sitting two to three lengths off him with energy to spare for the closing stages; Timely Affair, with three wins on similar going and proven course form, and Dannick, a course-and-distance winner also comfortable prominent, are best placed to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Arctician Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If the moderate early tempo suits Arctician's stamina so well that no tracker can close the gap in the straight.
scenarios.body: Arctician's 13-from-15 record on similar surfaces shows he handles the track better than most, and a field of hold-up types who cannot get their natural position will struggle to generate the late momentum needed to run him down.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swamps Field
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final two furlongs, creating a late sprint that allows a genuine closer to charge through from the back.
scenarios.body: Even in this scenario the redistributed hold-up horses — Madame De Sevigne, Lady Manzor, Moon Beginnings — are racing out of their natural position and may lack the last-furlong kick they need; Mollie Foster, who won over this course and trip, would be the most plausible beneficiary if gaps open late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Blanket Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Arctician fades and the pace completely collapses, triggering a scrambling finish with no clear tactical advantage.
scenarios.body: A compressed, multi-horse finish from the two-furlong pole would theoretically bring the whole pack into contention, but most runners here lack the finishing electricity on this surface to capitalise; Timely Affair's consistent placed efforts and Dannick's course win give them the narrowest edge in a chaotic conclusion.

watchPoints.text: Watch Timely Affair's early positioning — if Taylor Fisher pushes forward to sit second or third behind Arctician, she immediately becomes the most dangerous horse in the race given her three wins on similar going.

Arctician's early gallop is the race-defining variable — if James Glennon sends him clear at a genuinely slow tempo, the front-runner's chance moves sharply upward and hold-up horses become irrelevant.

Dannick and Timely Affair may both attempt to push forward from their draw, creating a brief scramble for the prominent positions in the first furlong; if they clash for the same ground behind Arctician, both could be compromised.

Moon Beginnings carries a fading-in-finish flag and has poor similar-going form — if she drifts wide in the straight searching for daylight, she is likely to be the horse who stops quickest and interferes with those coming from behind.

Mollie Foster's six consecutive sixths are a significant red flag, but note she won over exactly this course and trip — if pace collapses and gaps appear late, she is the one hold-up horse who has form to suggest she can finish through the field rather than around it.

races.name: Follow @AtTheRaces On X Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Recon Mission
runners_data.note: A 10-year-old hold-up specialist at OR 54 with Luke Morris aboard, he has placed twice from seven runs on similar going conditions but his recent form string shows mostly mid-pack or below finishes at 6f on Good ground, and today's drop to 5f AW Standard is his best trip profile for a late run.
runners_data.comment: Recon Mission is the top-rated runner in this field and shaped with promise when third last time out, returning refreshed after just 15 days; he has run over today's trip and going, and from stall one carries 134 lb, though the risk is that he remains winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Stapleford Park
runners_data.note: James Glennon (7lb claimer) rides this 4-year-old who is a true closer by nature but finds himself effectively racing in a midfield position given the concentration of hold-up types; Michael Attwater sends him in with one winner from thirteen runners over 14 days, and his single AW place on Standard ground is his most relevant piece of form.
runners_data.comment: Stapleford Park ran a fine second three starts back and returns on a quick turnaround of just 15 days, with experience of both today's trip and the going in his favour; the main risk is that he has been winless in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Coolagh Magic
runners_data.note: A 10-year-old veteran at OR 51 whose best recent form has come at 5-6f on Good and Soft turf, and while he has won over 6f on Good and placed over 5f on Standard AW, his true closer style is squeezed by a field that pushes him out of his natural deep position — William Carson has no recent trainer runners to draw on for confidence here.
runners_data.comment: Coolagh Magic won last time out and has experience of both today's trip and going, making him a clear threat on a retrieval run, though 57 days off the track is the question mark he must answer here.

runners_data.name: What A Tahoo
runners_data.note: A lightly-weighted 3-year-old at OR 53 with Ethan Tindall (5lb claimer) claiming, his form figures on Good ground at 5f are notably strong including two wins and a third, but he has not shown comparable form on AW Standard — as a natural hold-up type forced closer to the pace in this shape, his profile is compromised relative to a genuinely well-run sprint.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom but one on our figures and carrying a hefty 131 lb from stall 8, What A Tahoo faces a stiff ask, though she does bring winning form to the table — a winner two starts back — and has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Roman Spring
runners_data.note: A genuine prominent racer at OR 46 who has recent course exposure on Standard AW and is the most natural horse to slot in behind Harry Brown; Rachel Cook and John Bridger have one win from nine runners in the past 14 days, and he arrives on just 9 days rest, which could mean freshness or a quick turnaround risk.
runners_data.comment: Roman Spring has run over today's trip and going, and his consistency figures — fourth last time out, fifth two starts back, and third five starts back — hint at a horse that competes honestly, though he remains winless in his last six starts and his official mark of 46 leaves him with plenty still to prove.

runners_data.name: Nad Alshiba Snow
runners_data.note: A 4-year-old with Gina Mangan aboard who has the most extensive AW Standard form in the field across ten runs, yet no wins on this surface — her record shows she is placed on Standard conditions but her natural rearward style is constrained by the race shape today, and headgear (unspecified) is noted.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of eight on our figures, Nad Alshiba Snow has been winless in her last six starts, with a fifth last time out and a third four starts back her best recent efforts, making her very hard to fancy, though she does have experience over today's trip and going and returns fit on just 20 days' rest.

runners_data.name: Harry Brown
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner at OR 55 and top weight, he is the key pace ingredient — Tom Queally will likely use his natural pace to lead from the off on this flat 5f AW track, and his recent form includes a win and two places over the course and distance range; the STYLE_FIT flag reflects he is mapped as prominent in a field where he is more truly the lone leader, which slightly overstates pressure on him.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out and a winner six starts back, Harry Brown has been knocking on the door in recent starts and arrives here on a pleasing 23-day break, with experience of today's trip and conditions working in his favour at a competitive 135 lb.

runners_data.name: Dreambird Dolly
runners_data.note: Liam Wright (5lb claimer) partners this 4-year-old filly who has shown solid recent 5f form including a win and two seconds, wears a tongue-tie and blinkers, and represents the most dangerous hold-up threat if the pace is genuine; her OR of 54 keeps her competitive at the weights.
runners_data.comment: Dreambird Dolly has run over today's trip and going, and returns on a quick 15-day turnaround in decent nick — second two starts back and again three starts back hint at consistency, though she heads here ranked sixth of eight and has finished fifth on her most recent outing.

races.paceDynamic: Harry Brown is the sole confirmed front-runner and, on a flat 5f Lingfield AW surface with Standard ground, he is expected to take up his natural position unchallenged from the gates, setting a controlled, honest but not suicidal pace under Tom Queally. The field is loaded with hold-up horses — Stapleford Park, Coolagh Magic, What A Tahoo, Nad Alshiba Snow, and Recon Mission are all genuine closers — but with only Roman Spring as a secondary prominent type and no real rival to push Harry Brown, the pace is likely to be measured rather than frantic, which historically disadvantages pure hold-up horses on this sharp, flat track. Dreambird Dolly is a hold-up horse who has strong recent form at the trip and acts on AW, and she represents the most credible late threat if the pace stays honest enough to let her close. This race shape strongly favours prominent or just-off-the-pace runners who can travel in Harry Brown's slipstream and produce a sustained finish, rather than true deep closers who need a strong gallop to bridge the gap on a track that rarely punishes a front-runner dictating their own terms. The field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate — Stapleford Park, What A Tahoo, Coolagh Magic, and Nad Alshiba Snow are all genuine closers who will be forced to race closer to the pace than suits them, but Harry Brown and Roman Spring are best placed to secure the positions that matter.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Harry Brown Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Harry Brown is allowed to stride to the front uncontested and dictates a sustainable tempo on Standard ground.
scenarios.body: Harry Brown sets his own fractions with Tom Queally, keeps the pace honest enough to preserve his stamina reserves, and kicks clear from the 1f pole before deep closers can get organised off a modest gallop. Roman Spring, tracking just behind in a prominent position, is ideally placed to chase him down but the front-runner's advantage on this flat track is substantial.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Storm Late
scenarios.trigger: If Harry Brown's early pace is quicker than expected and the hold-up horses get a true run to close.
scenarios.body: A genuinely honest gallop on Standard AW compresses the field approaching the final furlong, giving horses like Dreambird Dolly and Recon Mission the fast-run race they need to close off a strong pace. Dreambird Dolly's recent 5f AW form, combined with Recon Mission's course experience and proven ability to finish strongly, makes them the chief beneficiaries if the race is run to suit closers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Roman Spring tracks Harry Brown tightly and produces a sharp, sustained challenge inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Roman Spring has shown course-specific form on this surface and, racing just off the pace in a small field, can sit in an ideal stalking position before producing a challenge that Harry Brown cannot repel. With closers likely to be racing out of their preferred deep hold-up role and failing to fully close, a prominent-tracking horse finishing with purpose has a clear path to the line.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and the race turns into a sprint from the 2f pole, shuffling the finishing order unpredictably.
scenarios.body: A slow early tempo causes bunching and a rough closing dash, which can produce an unlikely result but the redistributed hold-up horses — Stapleford Park, Coolagh Magic, What A Tahoo — are racing out of their natural roles and cannot reliably generate the finishing kick they would in a truly well-run race. This scenario is the least likely precisely because those horses who would normally profit are not operating in their true shape.

watchPoints.text: Harry Brown — watch whether Tom Queally allows him to coast into a soft lead or if Roman Spring pushes up alongside early; if Harry Brown is underpressured, the race could effectively be over at the 2f pole.

Dreambird Dolly — the 5lb claimer Liam Wright has to produce a well-timed late challenge from off the pace, and any traffic at the 1f pole on this tight track will cost her the race; she is the most likely closer to threaten if the pace is honest.

What A Tahoo and Stapleford Park — both are genuine hold-up horses running in an atypical position for this race shape; if either is caught wide without cover in the early stages they will burn energy they cannot afford at 5f.

Roman Spring — 9 days between runs is a quick turnaround, and though he arrives fit, watch whether he shows his usual early pace willingness at the gates; a sluggish break would leave Harry Brown completely unchallenged and shift the balance further toward the front.

Nad Alshiba Snow — ten runs on AW Standard without a win suggests a reliable but limited profile; she is unlikely to threaten the principals but her consistency means she could take minor honours if the pace-shape suits closers more than expected.
